the new isoforms of the TGF-beta R type II receptor are not differentially expressed in murine articular cartilage during aging and repair.
both TGF- beta RII isoforms are expressed by chandocytes in murine, bovine, and human articular chondryocytes.
the two isoforms TGF-beta R-II1 and TGFbeta R-II2 are differentially expressed in murine and in human chondrocyte.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a better understanding of the molecular basis of articular cartilage aging and the repair process.
the molecular mechanisms underlying the development of articular cartilage degeneration.
the identification and characterization of the TGF-beta receptor system in chondrocyte cultures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the relative mRNA expression pattern of the two Tgf-beta RII isoform does not seem to play an important role during cartilage repair or during aging.
the relative mRNA expression pattern of TGF-beta RI and TGF-beta RI2 is not altered during cartilage aging and repair.
both isoforms of TGF-beta receptor are expressed in murine articular cartilage and the relative mRNA expression is not affected by aging or mild PG depletion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that both isoforms of the TGF-beta receptor type II are expressed by murine and human chondrocyte.
TGF-beta R II2 seems to play an important role only in the cartilage of some mammals, but not in bovine cartilage.
the two isoforms are expressed in the cartilage and are not altered during aging or during repair processes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the relative expression of both TGF-beta receptor II isoforms remains unchanged during cartilage repair or during aging, suggesting that the differential TGF-beta response between normal cartilage undergoing repair is not the result of differences between the two isoforms.

the two isoforms are expressed in the same ratio in normal cartilage and during the repair phase and therefore it is unlikely that they play a role in age-related or repair-related TGF-beta signaling.
we have shown that the two isoforms are expressed in cartilage and that there are no age-related or cartilage repair-related differences in the relative levels of the two TGB-beta RII isoform.
